**The document doesn't give this number.** Per-position key-value retrieval results appear only in Figure 7 (p. 6), which is an image here, so I can't read values from it. The full results tables in Appendix G (p. 18) cover only the multi-document QA task.

The text does give some related figures:

- **Without query-aware contextualization**, the worst-case key-value retrieval performance is 45.6% (p. 7). The paper doesn't say which model, context length, or position this belongs to.
- **With query-aware contextualization** (the query placed before and after the key-value pairs), GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K) "achieves perfect performance when evaluated with 300 key-value pairs" (p. 7).
- GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K) is among the models with the lowest performance when the key is in the middle of the context. Models struggle most in the 140- and 300-pair settings (p. 6).

For the exact accuracy at position 200, you'd need to read it off Figure 7 or use the authors' released code and data (nelsonliu.me/papers/lost-in-the-middle, p. 2).
